c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: Two micro:bits talk over radio. What do they have to agree on?

B.text: A pairing code you type in

D.text: Nothing — radio finds the other board by itself

c1.why: The group is the whole agreement. There is no pairing step — boards on the same group hear each other.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: How many programs does this project need?

C.text: Two — one for the remote, one for the car

c2.why: The sender and the receiver do different jobs, so each board gets its own program.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: The remote sends the number 1. What does 1 mean to the radio?

A.text: Nothing — your receiver decides what it means

c3.why: The radio just carries a number. Meaning is something your receiving program adds.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: The remote sends 2. What does the car do?
r1.why: The second test matches, so the right-turn block runs.

r2.label: Q2
r2.why: The message arrives and the handler runs, but no test is true — so no block inside it does anything.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: The remote is on group 1 and the car on group 2. What happens when you press the remote?

D.text: Nothing — the car never hears it

r3.why: Different groups are different channels. The message is sent, but not to anyone listening on group 2.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: The remote sends 3 once and then nothing more. What does the car do?
r4.why: The block sets the motors going. Nothing tells them to stop, so a single message keeps the car moving.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: The car never responds to the remote at all. What is missing?
d1.why: Without a group set, the car is not listening on the channel the remote is using.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: Pressing A makes the car turn right instead of left. What is wrong?

D.text: The second test should be a different number

d2.why: Both branches match the same message, and the second one wins. Each command needs its own number.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Which blocks belong on the remote's program?

B.text: `on received number` and the drive blocks

b1.why: The remote's whole job is to join the channel and send. Driving belongs to the board that is bolted to the car.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: You want A+B to make the car go straight. On the remote, what does that button need?

A.text: A `send number` with a number the car does not use yet

b2.why: A third command needs a third number — and a matching branch on the car that gives that number a meaning.
